title: 5 months ago I built an AI interrogation game. 20K players later, I added a world strategy game mode
author: Own-Floor3521
selftext:
Solo dev. About five months ago I launched an interrogation and investigation game: you question AI suspects and work the evidence until the case cracks. It's grown to over 20K players and players have made 200+ cases of their own in the case builder.

After many of them played as detectives, I started getting similar feedback that they want to play as the criminals and gangsters. (No wonder GTA is so popular)

The new thing is a turn-based crime strategy game. You run one side of a real city: a detective bureau or a new crew in Los Angeles 1947, a yakuza family or the squad hunting them in Tokyo 1989, or a chaebol heir in Seoul 1995.

A night goes like this. You talk to people in plain text (your right hand, a cop who takes money, a rival's bookkeeper). You write orders the same way, like "have Lou take over the dice game on Skid Row, nobody gets hurt." Then you skip ahead and the night comes back as telegrams and a front page about what happened next.

And like the cases, players can now build worlds too: describe one in a sentence, it drafts a world you can edit, play and share.

It runs on Claude/Deepseek, in the browser. Free to start without an account and there are free daily credits! Longer games use a lot of credits, so you'll hit a paywall if you get hooked and I'd rather say that up front.

  
Any early feedback and comments will be great! 

[https://thelastquestion.io/world/noir](https://thelastquestion.io/world/noir)
